_what: One measured eval per decision a local judge model (records/local-model-records.json classify rows, such as decider-2b) might take, measured before any wiring (scripts/measure-decision-evals.mjs). Each eval names the decision, where it would be wired (`would_wire`), the words every case is asked as (`state`, filled from a case's values, and `question` with `means`), its labelled cases (`yes` is the right answer), and, when the decision already has an owner in source, that `incumbent` (a module export called with `args` filled from the case, whose result above 0 means yes). Cases marked held_out were written before the incumbent was last changed and were not looked at while changing it. When an eval has an incumbent, each judge is also measured behind it (`incumbent then <judge>`: the judge's score where the incumbent says yes, 0 where it says no), the shape of a server rule followed by a check on the person's Mac. A judge separates the cases when every yes case scores above every no case (`margin` above `separates_by`); only then is it a candidate for wiring. `last_measure` is written back by the script for each judge and the incumbent: right answers at the best cut, the cut, and the margin. A new decision is one row here.
